after.description: Where to go on from: the `next` of the page before, as the provider gave it; absent for the first page.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes a page holds: the caller's memory bound, never exceeded. A next line longer than it, line feed included, is refused, saying how long it is (see [`LINE_TOO_LARGE`](crate::LINE_TOO_LARGE)).

text.description: Whole JSON lines, each ended by a line feed. Only the first page starts with the header.

next.description: What to ask for the next page with ([`SessionExport::after`]); absent when the export is complete.

program.description: The program: a path, or a name looked up on the `PATH` where it runs, the spec's own `PATH` when its environment sets one.

args.description: Its arguments, one element each, never re-split by a shell.

cwd.description: Its working directory, by the rules of where it runs; the spawner's choice when absent.

environment.description: Variables set over the spawner's own environment, or over none with `clear_environment`.

clear_environment.description: Starts from no variables at all rather than the spawner's own.

remove_environment.description: Variables taken out of the spawner's own environment before `environment` is set.

terminal.description: A terminal of this size for its input and output, standard error included; plain pipes when absent.

x-enum-labels.separate: Its own stream, read with [`SpawnedProcess::read_error`]: standard output then carries only what the program wrote there, as a JSON-lines harness needs.

error_output.description: Where standard error goes, with pipes.

title.description: Its name for people, such as `Claude Code`.

versions.description: The ACP versions its `initialize` answers, lowest first.

mcp_sse.description: MCP servers reached over server-sent events.

load.description: `session/load`: a session reopened with its history replayed.

resume.description: `session/resume`: a session reopened without its history replayed.

additional_directories.description: More directories than the working one.

system_prompt.description: A system prompt appended to the harness's own.

resumes_wider.description: Whether a session held to requirements can be reopened (`session/load` or `session/resume`) on a later connection started with fewer, and then have what that connection allows.

x-enum-labels.inferred: Read from an error's words, a 429 or a refusal, by the provider or the host. The bucket's `evidence` holds the words, for logs; nothing parses it.

sources.description: Which kinds of figure it can give.

needs_turn.description: Whether it learns its usage only during a turn. Then a read with no turn answers what the connection last saw, and a host keeps a timed retry instead of polling for fresh figures. `false` means [`USAGE_METHOD`] re-reads the account each time, so a host may poll it.

needs_session.description: Whether it learns its usage only once a session is open, though no turn is needed (an agent that serves its figures from the process a session starts). With none open, a read answers what the connection last saw, and nothing is started for it.

usage.description: What usage it reports, and so whether its `initialize` advertises the usage extension.

known.description: Whether the harness listed them; when not, `models` is empty.

code.description: Its exit code, when it exited by itself.

signal.description: The signal that ended it, on Unix.

drops.description: How many times it has gone down since the process started: a reader that sees the count grow knows its output paused.
